key_insight: SrLaCoNbO6 shows strong spin-lattice coupling with Raman and EXAFS anomalies well above its antiferromagnetic transition, consistent with fluctuating Kitaev-like magnetic interactions.
engineering_relevance: The results matter for designing quantum and magnetic oxide materials where local lattice distortions and spin dynamics must be controlled together.
method: Temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy to track phonon shifts, linewidths, Fano asymmetry, and continuum features.
Co K-edge EXAFS to probe local bond lengths and Debye-Waller factors around Co ions.
Correlation of spectral anomalies with magnetic and structural temperature scales.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports phonon and local-structure anomalies near 60 K and 160–180 K, plus a broad low-energy Raman continuum that is excitation-energy independent.
watch_item: The observed anomalies may include a structural contribution, so the magnetic interpretation is suggestive rather than definitive without additional complementary measurements.
paper_title: Raman spectroscopic signature of Kitaev magnetism and complex spin-lattice coupling in S = 1/2 antiferromagnet SrLaCoNbO$_6$ double perovskite
